newsitem.title: UK: Russia wants Eurobond to give it respectability.
newsitem.headline: Russia wants Eurobond to give it respectability.

text.p: Russia's Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Friday he wanted the country's debut Eurobond to show it was a respectable borrower.

"The purpose for entering this market is not a short-term goal, it is for the long term," Livshits said at a news conference held before meeting London-based investors to drum up support for the bond issue.
"We want from the outset to look respectable and the cost of borrowing is a very important factor for us," he said, adding reports Russia would pay an 11 percent coupon were "ridiculous".
"We will not borrow on very high interest levels - this is not our purpose at all," Livshits said.
Earlier this week finance ministry officials said in Moscow they expected Russia would have to pay between 10 and 11 percent for the Eurobond.
Terms of the deal, expected to be for up to $500 million for between three and five years, would not be determined until presentations had been completed in New York on November 20.
Three teams of senior Russian officials have been travelling the globe this week to market the deal, Russia's first visit to the international capital markets since the 1917 revolution.
"The results so far seem quite satisfactory," Livshits said. "The response (from investors) has been warm and they liked what we presented," he said.
The Eurobond would allow Russia to diversify sources of funding for the state budget deficit and would open up the international markets for other Russian borrowers.
Another goal was to discover what international investors thought Russian securities were worth. "We have a number of different goals, and we expect the project to be successful," Livshits said.
Another aim was to see whether the interest paid internationally would be different to that paid on domestic securities.
"We want to show to ourselves we do not overpay in the internal (domestic bond) market," Livshits said.
"The results of the bond will carry serious signals for domestic investors. We believe the Eurobond will have a positive effect on the domestic market in 1997," he said.
International borrowing was expected to continue next year but would not replace domestic debt issuance.
"In 1997 the government would like to borrow on the international market as a reliable and sustainable source of borrowing," Livshits said.
"But in spite of this the general approach will not be to change the general approach. The internal market will remain the main source of funds," he said.
